title: Asynchronous
body:
No shared clock. In [[Sequential Logic]], an asynchronous circuit changes state as soon as
its inputs do, rather than waiting for an edge, which makes it fast and hard to reason
about. In [[Serial I-O]], asynchronous means the line only sends when there is data, so
each byte carries its own start and stop bits to tell the receiver where it begins. That
is the **A** in [[UART]].

Sampling an asynchronous signal with a [[Synchronous]] circuit risks
[[metastability]]. See also [[Asynchronous Handshaking]].

---

This note is about **digital logic and serial lines**: no shared clock. The other sense of the
word, **asynchronous programming** (work started now and finishing later, so the value is not
available on the next line), belongs to [[Asynchronous JS]] in [[WEB DEVELOPMENT FOR CS]].
They are different subjects that share a word, in the same way [[Complexity]], [[FIFO]], and
[[Status Register]] do.

The connection, if you want one: both mean "not lockstep with something else". Here it is a
clock edge; there it is the main thread of execution. Neither definition helps you read the
other's code.
